claims.text: Clinical diagnosis and treatment of child and adolescent psychiatric disorders increased over recent decades.
Epidemiological comparisons of unselected population cohorts using equivalent assessments find little evidence of an increased rate of ADHD.
There is substantial secular change in emotional problems in high-income countries, including periods of increase and decrease in symptom prevalence.
There is substantial secular change in antisocial behaviour in high-income countries, including periods of increase and decrease in symptom prevalence.
Cross-cohort comparisons can provide valuable complementary information on the aetiology of mental illness.

evidence.description: Clinical diagnosis and treatment of child and adolescent psychiatric disorders increased over recent decades.
Epidemiological comparisons of unselected population cohorts using equivalent assessments of mental health have found little evidence of an increased rate of ADHD.
Findings do suggest substantial secular change in emotional problems and antisocial behaviour in high-income countries, including periods of increase and decrease in symptom prevalence.

methodologies.name: Systematic literature review of epidemiological cross-cohort comparisons
methodologies.description: Evaluates population prevalence trends in child and adolescent mental health problems using systematic searches of cross-cohort epidemiological literature.

limitations.text: Cross-cohort comparisons of rates of ASD are lacking at this time.
Evidence from low- and middle-income countries is very limited.
